evidence.says: LC heading is Morgan, Kenneth, 1953-. Its publisher-information note dated December 23, 2003 gives the full name Kenneth John Morgan and birth year 1953. Other notes identify Brunel University, the 1984 Oxford thesis on Bristol merchants and colonial trade, Bristol and the Atlantic Trade in the Eighteenth Century (1993), and Fritz Reiner, Maestro and Martinet (2004). The same record inconsistently encodes 1956 in the structured birthDate field.

Describes Kenneth Morgan as a historian born in 1953, with alias Kenneth John Morgan and employer Brunel University London. Identifiers include LC n2003148649, BnF 12417140j, VIAF 98067967 and ISNI 0000000115788847; the birth statement cites BnF.

BnF identifies Morgan, Kenneth (1953-....), variant Kenneth John Morgan, as a professor of history at Brunel University. It gives birth year 1953, ISNI 0000000115788847, and cites Bristol and the Atlantic Trade in the Eighteenth Century (1993) and The Birth of Industrial Britain (2004).

The graph's Open Library author identifier lists Bristol and the Atlantic Trade in the Eighteenth Century, Bristol Merchants and the Colonial Trades, 1748-1783, Fritz Reiner, Maestro and Martinet, and Proscription by Degrees, matching LC works and thesis subject. The list also contains other titles whose attribution is not established by this check.

notes: The birth warning arises from an internal LC discrepancy: its structured birth year is 1956, but its heading and publisher-supplied source note support 1953, corroborated by BnF. Matching name forms, affiliation, identifiers and works establish the same person. LC HTML was inaccessible; its official linked-data JSON was read. Wikidata was available through indexed page content. The graph-key match rests on the matching Open Library works; its bare dissertation citation supplies no further distinction.
